jobs.occupation: (Senior) Project Manager/Process Specialist, Drug Substance Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with outsourced chemical manufacturing of starting materials, intermediates and APIs? Are you passionate about science-driven development and manufacturing support in collaboration with contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs)?

_If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new (Senior) Project Manager or Process Specialist.

_

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a skilled project manager/specialist to join our growing team. As a key member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in our team for commercial chemical manufacturing for projects having reached the stage of process qualification and commercial manufacturing. The manufacturing processes comprise peptide synthesis, peptide conjugation and purification and classic organic chemistry for small molecules and polymers. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will be joining the Chemical Manufacturing team consisting of 6 colleagues, and report directly to Birgitte M. Malle, Senior Directorwho is based in Hellerup_._ You will be based in Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Manage and coordinate outsourced commercial manufacture of peptides, chemical starting materials, intermediates and APIs including technology transfer, process validation (PPQ), post PPQ optimizations, risk management, control strategies and continuous process verification programs (CPV)

• Trouble shooting in collaboration with CMO's including Deviation and Change management as subject matter expert

• Support master batch record update and release of batches together with QA

• Write and support regulatory submissions for marketing approval and post-approval

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a Master of Science or a Ph.D. in organic chemistry, peptide synthesis, chemical engineering or equivalent - and have at least 5 years of experience within pharmaceutical development or manufacturing industry.

Furthermore, you have:

• Relevant hands-on experience from laboratory, pilot and/or manufacturing facilities

• GMP experience

• Proficient English professional skills

• MS Office skills including experience with SAS JMP or other data management tools

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player, have attention to details, and have a can-do attitude.

You possess an entrepreneurial mindset and can thrive in an informal, open environment where innovation and change are key.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to be a highly motivated individual who enjoys being challenged and working in collaborative environments. Strong interpersonal skills are necessary as your job is to establish and maintain good and productive collaboration with CMO's. A proven ability to communicate with stakeholders of other functions and disciplines is crucial.

Travel: up to 10-15 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Senior Director for Chemical Manufacturing, Birgitte M. Malle, bmm@ascendispharma.com

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

jobs.description:

You will help turn technical requirements and design into practical, high-quality installation solutions and ensure efficient production throughout all phases of shipbuilding, in compliance with naval and classification standards. Your work will have a direct impact on the successful delivery of the Arctic ships and on the continued development of the Danish naval shipbuilding industry.

Your tasks & responsibilities 

As Senior Electrical Engineer, Technical Lead you will plan, coordinate, and lead the electrical installation scope throughout ship production, ensuring alignment between engineering, procurement, suppliers, and production teams.

jobs.occupation: Mechanical Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Mechanical Design Engineer: Develop robust medical devices from concept to production

Would you like to use your mechanical engineering expertise to develop medical devices that make a real difference for people with intimate healthcare needs?

Working with engineers, scientists and project managers, you will turn product requirements and concepts into robust mechanical solutions, combining creative problem-solving with engineering rigour from concept evaluation through to production.

Welcome to CC & BC Mechanical Engineering

At our headquarters in Humlebæk, Denmark, you will join CC & BC Mechanical Engineering within Product Development, developing products for Continence Care and Bowel Care.

Mechanical design connects what users need with how a product performs and how reliably it can be manufactured. Our work brings together functionality, materials, tolerances and production considerations to create practical solutions that perform consistently in everyday use.

You will work closely with colleagues across Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, Technical Design, Materials, Systems Engineering, Usability and Test Engineering, as well as Manufacturing Systems Development and Centre of Excellence specialists.

Turn product concepts into reliable, manufacturable solutions

As our new Mechanical Design Engineer, you will plan and deliver mechanical design activities in Product Development projects. Your work will span concept development and evaluation, detailed design, verification support and transfer to production.

You will take ownership of your mechanical deliverables and provide clear technical conclusions and recommendations. Working within the agreed project scope, you will identify risks early, make design trade-offs visible and bring in the right expertise to move decisions forward.

More specifically, you will:

•    Develop and evaluate mechanical concepts, translating product requirements into practical design solutions in collaboration with Systems Engineering and relevant specialists.

•    Develop and document mechanical designs using 3D CAD, working closely with Technical Design on drawings and specifications.

•    Apply robust design methods and tolerance analysis to understand variation and secure reliable product performance.

•    Apply Design for X principles to balance performance, manufacturability, sustainability and cost, involving manufacturing specialists early.

•    Use calculations, simulation, prototypes and test evidence to evaluate solutions and support timely design decisions.

•    Contribute mechanical expertise to risk assessments, verification planning, technical reviews and design documentation.

•    Plan and deliver your activities against agreed project commitments, communicating risks, dependencies and the impact of proposed changes early.

•    Share technical learning and help improve mechanical design practices across projects.

A mechanical engineer with practical judgement and a collaborative approach

You enjoy both exploring concepts and working through the details that make a design reliable. You can turn analysis into clear recommendations, explain design trade-offs and challenge unclear assumptions constructively.

You take a structured approach without making solutions more complex than necessary. You understand when further analysis is needed and when the available evidence supports moving forward. Above all, you take responsibility for your work while recognising that strong product solutions depend on contributions from several disciplines.

We imagine that you:

•    Hold a BSc or MSc in mechanical engineering, mechanical design, product development or a related discipline.

•    Have experience developing mechanical solutions, including plastic components for injection moulding and high-volume production.

•    Work confidently with 3D CAD, preferably SolidWorks.

•    Have experience with robust design, tolerance calculations and design for manufacture.

•    Can apply engineering theory, calculations and data analysis to practical design challenges.

•    Communicate technical ideas and conclusions clearly, both visually and verbally.

•    Work effectively across disciplines and document your work clearly.

•    Communicate confidently in English.

Experience in medical devices or another regulated industry is an advantage. We also value experience with simulation and an interest in using digital tools, including AI where relevant, to improve engineering analysis and development efficiency.

You do not need to know every method from the outset. Curiosity, sound engineering judgement and a willingness to develop your expertise are important.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Jesper Bruun Jensen, Head of Continence Care & Bowel Care Mechanical Engineering, at DKJBRJ@coloplast.com.

We review applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager in the Climate and Energy Policy Division - DTU Management
jobs.description:
We are pleased to announce an opportunity for joining the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as a project manager in the Climate and Energy Policy Division, at the Department of Technology, Management and Economics – in short DTU Management. 

We are looking for a skilled and experienced project manager with knowledge about energy systems and planning, who will help manage and support several new research projects funded by EU and Danida. 

Responsibilities
The job will include organisation of project meetings, dissemination activities, data handling and management, and different administrative support to our projects. 

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Take responsibility and support for project deliverables, technical reporting and milestone monitoring in EU projects.
• Foster project synergies and collaborations across our projects consortia and stakeholders to meet EU requirements for deliverables and reporting.
• Contribute to project governance, project performance, and project-specific decision-making across our projects. 
• Administrative support to our Energy Planning course, funded by Danida
• Contribute to the projects’ scientific dissemination and research communication in the consortium projects for the stakeholders.
• Handling of data in some of the projects
• Write project deliverables for scientific reporting and prepare for publications in collaboration with the consortium.
Our expectations of you
We are looking for a talented colleague who delivers results through positive and effective teamwork. You should thrive in an interdisciplinary, multicultural, and highly collaborative environment, where knowledge sharing and cooperation are key to success.

We expect that you have:

• A relevant master’s degree (or equivalent)
• Practical experience with project management and dissemination 
• Experience with handling different types of data
• Knowledge on energy systems and planning
• Experience with Microsoft Suite software and LaTeX collaborative environment 
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international atmosphere with the focus on research, teaching, innovation and scientific advice for the benefit of the surrounding community. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. In the area of technical and natural sciences, DTU is one of the leading research and education institutions in Europe.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Employee. 

In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The position is a full-time position for 2 years. The start date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). 

The workplace is DTU Lyngby Campus.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Section, Professor Dogan Keles (dogke@dtu.dk) or Senior Researcher Per Sieverts Nielsen (pernn@dtu.dk). 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. You can read more about the Department at DTU Management.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Who are we?
DTU Management conducts excellent research at the intersection of management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master, and PhD levels across DTU's study programs. The department has 250+ employees with around half of staff coming from abroad. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: 171626 Associate professor in Clinical Proteomics and Data-Driven Biomarker Discovery for Neurodegenerative Disease (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position: 

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Desired qualifications: 

   	
• Strong, independent research record in neurodegenerative disease, with expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and biofluid biomarker discovery. 	
• Experience integrating multi-omics data with machine learning and AI, and working with preclinical models and cell-type-resolved approaches. 	
• A track record of securing competitive external funding and of research leadership. 	
• Teaching experience and formal teaching qualifications (e.g. Universitetspædagogikum), together with supervision experience. 	
• Ability to bridge discovery and translation (from molecule to patient) and to collaborate across academia, clinic, and industry, including innovation and spin-out activity   Terms of employment
 The position is a time limited position for 5 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.
 
 Questions
 For further information, please contact Head of Department Dan Stærk, ds@sund.ku.dk. For information about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND), please see www.drug.ku.dk and https://sund.ku.dk/.

  
 Foreign applicants may find this link useful: https://www.ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility).
 
 Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application, including motivations for applying for the position (maximum 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• Research plan (3-5 pages) 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 (associate professors) publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/job-application-portfolio)   Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at The university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) engineering: internalization and lysosomal delivery
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC) / Finsen Laboratory, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  A 3-year PhD fellowship is available in the research group of Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm. Expected start: 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project

  Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on efficient internalization and lysosomal processing to release their cytotoxic payload. Inefficient trafficking limits potency and restricts current ADCs to targets with very high receptor density. The PhD project will engineer and test next-generation ADCs with improved internalization and lysosomal routing. This includes bispecific constructs that combine our established ADC targets (uPAR, MMP14, uPARAP and the Mannose Receptor) with receptors that drive lysosomal delivery, such as IGF2R. Lead candidates will be evaluated in cancer cell models and in vivo, including models of sarcoma and glioblastoma.

  The project is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Distinguished Innovator project "Breaking Barriers: Engineering ADCs for Efficient BBB Transport and Lysosomal Targeting", in collaboration with Professor Matthias Herth (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, UCPH) and Professor Katrine Qvortrup (Department of Chemistry, DTU).

   

  Main tasks

   	
•  	Production, purification and validation of recombinant and bispecific antibodies

 	 	
•  	Conjugation of antibodies to cytotoxic payloads and characterization of the resulting ADCs

 	 	
•  	Cell-based assays: antibody uptake and internalization, flow cytometry, drug screening and cytotoxicity/cell viability assays

 	 	
•  	In vivo efficacy studies of ADC candidates in tumor models

 	 	
•  	Writing scientific publications and presenting at international conferences

 	    

   

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
•  	Carrying through an independent research project under supervision. 

 	 	
•  	Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points.

 	 	
•  	Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team.

 	 	
•  	Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project

 	 	
•  	Teaching and disseminating your knowledge.

 	 	
•  	Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project

 	    

  PhD Programme Description:
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., [relevant degrees]).

   

  Qualifications

  We are looking for a candidate with a strong, hands-on background in ADC research. Applicants must have:

   	
•  	An MSc degree (120 ECTS, or equivalent) in pharmaceutical biotechnology, biotechnology or a closely related field, with an excellent academic record

 	 	
•  	An MSc thesis or equivalent research project on antibody-drug conjugates or antibody-based cancer therapeutics

 	 	
•  	Documented hands-on experience with production, validation and payload conjugation of recombinant antibodies

 	 	
•  	Experience with cytotoxicity, cell viability and drug screening assays in mammalian cancer cell lines

 	 	
•  	Experience with flow cytometry

 	 	
•  	Experience with laboratory animal work

 	 	
•  	Experience from an international research laboratory and excellent written and spoken English

 	   Experience with functional genomics (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 screening) and with sarcoma models is an advantage.

     Place of employment

  The place of employment is BRIC, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. 

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 15 January 2027 or after agreement.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

jobs.description:
European Doctoral Network – WindConnect | DTU Wind and Energy Systems | Fully funded · 36 months.

Shape the future of hybrid renewable power plants
Join the Renewable Power Plants (RPP) section at DTU Wind and Energy Systems and help shape the next generation of control systems for hybrid wind, solar, and battery power plants. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in power systems and renewable energy integration, who are motivated by developing technical, practical solutions to complex real-world challenges and thrive in a highly international and collaborative research environment.

In this fully funded three-year PhD project, you will develop an innovative, technology-agnostic control architecture for hybrid power plants, combining advanced modelling with opportunities for experimental validation in collaboration with European Energy.

The position is part of the WindConnect European Doctoral Network, bringing together 15 PhD researchers across leading European universities and industry partners to advance the next generation of wind energy technology.

Why choose this PhD?

• Unique experimental infrastructure. In close collaboration with European Energy, you will gain hands-on exposure to DTU's MW-scale hybrid power plant research facility, one of only a few such testbeds worldwide. The facility offers opportunities to explore your control concepts in a realistic operational environment, subject to feasibility and access.
• European research community. As part of WindConnect, you will join a vibrant network of 15 doctoral researchers, collaborate with leading academic and industry partners across Europe, and undertake 6-9 months of research stays at partner institutions.
• High-impact research. Your work will help hybrid renewable power plants provide reliable grid services and support the transition to power systems with higher shares of wind and solar energy, with potential implications for grid operators, plant developers, and energy policy.
• Broad career development. Benefit from technical and transferable-skills training, industrial secondments, international conference participation, peer-reviewed publications, and a strong professional network across academia and industry.
About the project
Hybrid Power Plants (HPPs), combining wind, solar PV, and battery energy storage behind a single grid connection point, are emerging as a cornerstone of future power systems. While they can provide grid services beyond the capabilities of individual technologies, coordinating assets from different vendors with varying response times and communication protocols remains a major challenge. Traditional control architectures struggle to reconcile fast local asset responses with slower plant-level actions, while communication delays and interoperability issues add further complexity.

This PhD project addresses these challenges by developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale HPPs. The architecture is designed to improve interoperability, reduce communication overhead, and enhance the reliability and performance of hybrid power plants.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale hybrid power plants (HPPs) integrating wind, solar PV, and battery storage. The architecture will enable direct communication between the HPP controller and individual asset controllers while addressing interoperability challenges across technologies and vendors. You will design control solutions that coordinate fast local responses with plant-level objectives. The work will combine controller design, high-fidelity modelling and simulation, and, where feasible, experimental evaluation in collaboration with European Energy.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Model and benchmark state-of-the-art HPP control architectures, including dynamic behaviour and grid-service performance.
• Identify interoperability, communication, and coordination challenges across assets, vendors, and control layers.
• Design and implement a two-layer controller that connects fast local responses with plant-wide coordination.
• Evaluate the proposed architecture using high-fidelity modelling and simulation (e.g. MATLAB/Simulink and Python) and, where feasible, explore experimental testing at DTU's hybrid power plant facility.
• Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to IEA Wind Task 50 on Hybrid Power Plants.
• Participate in WindConnect training activities and provide limited support for MSc supervision and teaching at DTU.
What we are looking for

Essential qualifications

• MSc degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in electrical engineering, power system engineering, control engineering, or a related field.
• Sound fundamentals in power-system dynamics and control, with an understanding of converter-interfaced generation and storage.
• Experience with dynamic modelling and simulation using tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, Python, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD or comparable software.
• Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to conduct independent research
Advantageous (nice to have qualifications)

• Familiarity with grid integration requirements, ancillary service provision, and/or multi-vendor renewable power plant control.
• Experience in international or cross-disciplinary research collaborations.
• Strong English communication and interpersonal skills for effective collaboration in international and multidisciplinary teams.
What we offer

• A fully funded 3-year PhD position at DTU, offering co-supervision by experienced researchers and close collaboration with European Energy and leading industry partners in an internationally recognised research environment.
• A collegial, diverse, and inclusive research environment that invests in your development, well-being, and career growth through international networking, multidisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and partnerships with leading universities and industry across Europe.
• Diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds. 
MSCA eligibility – please check before applying

This position is funded through the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) European Doctoral Network. To be eligible, applicants must:

• Not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment.
• Have less than four years of full-time equivalent research experience after obtaining the degree that qualifies them for PhD studies.
• Not have resided or carried out their main activity (work or studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.
Please note: Applicants who do not meet these MSCA eligibility criteria cannot be considered for the position, regardless of their qualifications. Please verify your eligibility before applying. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds.
Salary and appointment terms

Further information

You can read more at wind.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure

jobs.occupation: One or more Professors in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for one or more professors in the field of Cyber Security as per March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The positions are permanent.

**Who we are

**In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems is ranked among the top 50 in the world in the Shanghai Ranking (GRAS). The department employs more than 200 people, of whom approximately 90 are PhD students, and around 40% of all employees are international. In total, the department has more than 800 students enrolled in its BSc and MSc programmes, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and laboratory facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and research results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department here www.es.aau.dk.

The Cyber Security Research Group at Aalborg University (Cyber Security Research Group) is a young and growing research group within the Department of Electronic Systems, focusing on cyber security from various perspectives. Its core research areas are network security, IoT/OT security, applied cryptography, and privacy and security in machine learning. The Cyber Security Research Group consists of 16 members and offers a young, international research environment. The group is responsible for teaching activities in the Master’s programme in Cyber Security, which is taught in English and has more than 100 active Danish and international students. Moreover, the group is strongly engaged in community-building activities, with the AAU Copenhagen campus serving as a hub for weekly CTFs and ethical hacking activities involving dozens of participants.

Your work tasks

You will lead the academic direction of cyber security research and education. The role combines independent academic leadership with close collaboration across the department, within the section, with other research environments, external organisations, and international partners.

Your research and teaching will address one or more areas within applied cryptography, IoT and/or cloud security, security and privacy for big data and machine learning, risk management and threat modelling, mobile security, secure software development, and systems security and privacy. You will initiate and lead research projects, secure and manage external research funding, publish research at an international level, and develop collaborations with industry, public-sector organisations, and universities in Denmark and abroad.

You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, develop courses and teaching materials, and contribute to the planning and coordination of programmes built on problem-based learning. You will also supervise doctoral researchers and early-career colleagues, contribute to relevant committees and academic activities, and take part in developing the department’s research and educational priorities. International collaboration, including participation in networks, conferences, and joint research activities, forms an integral part of the position.

Your competencies

You hold a doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. You have documented original research contributions at an international level within cyber security and a strong publication record in recognised journals and conferences. You can demonstrate a proven track record of attracting, establishing, and managing externally funded research activities, and you have the academic judgement required to develop a coherent research agenda with clear societal and technological relevance.

You bring substantial experience in university teaching, supervision, course development, examination activities, and the development of educational programmes. Familiarity with problem-based learning is relevant, particularly because the role includes contributing to programmes in which students work collaboratively on complex and practice-oriented challenges. You communicate confidently in English, both orally and in writing, and you are willing to develop Danish language skills over time.

You set a clear academic direction while creating constructive working relationships with students, colleagues, and collaborators. You contribute with sound judgement, curiosity, and an ability to turn research ideas into well-organised projects and partnerships. You support the development of early-career researchers, engage openly across disciplines, and help maintain a respectful and collaborative research culture.

**Qualification requirements

**Applicants must be able to document a high degree of original academic production at an international level and experience from teaching at different levels. Including tests/exams, course/study programme management as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material.

Emphasis is placed on the extent, to which the applicant, has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.

Emphasis may moreover be placed on the applicant’s ability to carry out and develop research-based public-sector consultancy. Also, emphasis will be placed on an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks and possibly fulfil other functions, for example in relation to the university’s external cooperation.

Emphasis will also be placed on the applicant's ability to undertake pedagogical supervision, supervision and academic assessment work.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Professor”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
